title: Maximum Side Length of a Square with Sum Less than or Equal to Threshold
statement:
You are given an `m x n` grid of non-negative integers `mat` and an integer `threshold`. Consider every square block of cells inside the grid (its rows and its columns are each a contiguous run of the same length `k`, with `k >= 1`).

Return the largest side length `k` of such a square whose cells add up to at most `threshold`. When no square qualifies (every single cell is already larger than `threshold`), return `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

Summing every square cell by cell costs far too much on a 300 by 300 grid. A 2D prefix-sum table answers "what is the total of this block?" in O(1) with four lookups. On top of that, the answer can grow by at most one per cell: if we already found a square of side `best`, the only useful question at a new bottom-right corner is whether a square of side `best + 1` ends there. Because all values are non-negative, a valid square of side K contains valid smaller squares along its diagonal, so this one-step-at-a-time growth always reaches the true answer.

## Approach

1. Build `prefix` with an extra zero row and column; `prefix[i][j]` is the total of the top-left `i x j` block.
2. Visit cells in row-major order. Fill `prefix[i][j]` from the cell value and its three neighbours in the table.
3. Let `side = best + 1`. If a square of that side fits with its bottom-right corner at `(i, j)`, get its `sum` from four prefix values.
4. If `sum <= threshold`, set `best = side`.
5. Return `best` (it stays 0 when no single cell fits).

## Example 1, step by step

`threshold = 4`, three identical rows `[1, 1, 3, 2, 4, 3, 2]`.

- At `(1, 1)` the 1 by 1 square holds `1 <= 4`, so `best = 1`.
- The rest of row 1 cannot host a 2 by 2 square. At `(2, 2)` the 2 by 2 square holds `1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4 <= 4`, so `best = 2`.
- A 3 by 3 square only fits in row 3; the cheapest one (columns 1 to 3) already sums to `15`, so `best` stays `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n): each cell does a constant amount of work.
- Space: O(m · n) for `prefix`.

## Pitfalls

- Off-by-one errors in the prefix table: the padded row and column make `prefix[i - side][...]` safe when the square touches the top or left edge.
- The block sum is `prefix[i][j] - prefix[i - side][j] - prefix[i][j - side] + prefix[i - side][j - side]`; forgetting to add back the corner subtracts it twice.
- Return `0`, not `1`, when every cell is larger than `threshold`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | the grid's size |
| `prefix` | padded 2D prefix sums of `mat` |
| `best` | largest valid side found so far |
| `i`, `j` | bottom-right corner in prefix coordinates (1-based) |
| `side` | the side length being tried, `best + 1` |
| `sum` | total of the candidate square |
